seat.BEST_WHY: The upper wall's timber lintel (the band at y≈430–450 running the full width of the room) is the best-made element in the deck: a beam with driven pins at uneven spacing (≈x300, 380, 455, 590), a darker shadow band under it that cleanly separates wall top from floor, and a right-hand break where the beam stops and the corridor mouth opens. The flagstones under the figure vary in size and joint width (one large block at ≈540–620,480–540 next to half-blocks at ≈450,520), so they read as laid rather than stamped. The tied log bundle at ≈440,615 is a rope-bound stack of salvaged timber — it is the only prop in the deck that actually shows the fiction's repair method. Light from the figure and the brazier both fall onto the floor and mix warm-over-cool without a hard seam between them.
seat.WORST_WHY: Flat, unlit, and stamped. There is no light carrier falloff at all — every corner of the frame is at the same value, so the brief's one stated lighting rule is absent. The grey block walls (left column x<50, bottom band y>200) are one brick tile repeated with no top/face distinction and a hard tone change at ≈50,105 where two wall tiles of different grey meet mid-run. The dirt floor shows its repeat: the same small blue-grey speck cluster reappears on a grid (≈130,45 / 185,155 / 235,155). The pool is a flat green fill with one lily-pad sprite duplicated three times (≈320,25 / 330,115 / 270,165) and one blob sprite duplicated at ≈310,110 and 270,165. Two identical barrels at ≈130,200 / 175,200, two identical chests at ≈80,15 / 80,60. The bottom wall band is cut mid-brick at the frame edge with a lighter dash at ≈170,278 that doesn't belong to the pattern. It reads as an asset-pack placeholder.

flip_list: Move the A-frame timber at ≈630,390: it sits on the top surface of the upper wall above the lintel, not on floor, and casts no contact shadow — place it on floor tiles and add a contact shadow.
Move or crop the crossed timber at ≈260,675: it straddles the boundary between lit floor and the dark tile below the standing slab, so half of it is at floor value and half is not.
The standing slab at ≈280,585 is a flat pale rectangle with a two-tone edge and a tiny dark base; give it a top face vs. side face and a cast shadow toward the side away from the figure.
Remove or explain the dark square at ≈315–370,650–710: it is a single tile of a different, darker floor texture with hard edges inside the lit area and reads as a mis-tiled cell.

The crack lines (e.g. the one running ≈230,520 → 330,560 → 400,640, and the long arc ≈560,690 → 750,640) are continuous 1px lines that cross flagstone joints and the wall/floor boundary without breaking; a crack in laid stone follows or stops at joints — break them at every joint and drop the ones crossing onto wall.

The flagstone hatching is at screen-pixel resolution while the figure is at ≈3× pixel scale; the floor reads as a brush texture under a pixel sprite. Redraw the floor hatch at the sprite's pixel density.
The dark corridor tops (≈100–400,100–350) are a soft cloudy blur with 1px crack lines over it; replace the blur with a drawn stone-top tile at the same pixel density as the wall face.
The brazier at ≈600,545 lights the floor but not the wall beside it: the wall face at ≈650–750,450 is at the same value as the unlit wall at ≈200,450 despite being closer to the fire.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

Marker content 10x15 px in a 32 px cell — a fifth of the cell, twenty device pixels across; three cold seats offered 'a bottle or vial', 'a lantern or candle', 'an orange chest or crate' for the marker and 'sticks' for the barricade. _what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
item_exit.item: #212 round 2 — the Λ-frame against the north wall: 'feet land on the cap band, not below it; no reveal foot visible under it. Also brighter and more saturated than the X-frame under the same fire' (Rafe, props walk, 2026-09-13)
item_exit.claim: a prop placed against a wall stands on the floor at the reveal's foot, in front of the face, and is never overdrawn by the cap; the barricade family is one wood, and every lit difference between its members is the rig's.
item_exit.measured: MEASURED BEFORE BUILDING (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/jamb/, m_flat + jamb_m_shadow). (a) The sprite's bottom wood row sat at frame y 544 against a reveal foot at 546/547 — the SPRITE was at the foot, as the report said; the EYE was right too, because §3.2's base parallelogram rises ½·0.35·cell = 11 px up-right from that row (ReviewLighting's occluder draws exactly it), so the whole footprint lay over the FACE: feet inside the wall. (b) The cap's upper half was re-laid over the prop (cap_bands_over_props=2) — the law says never. (c) Flat-lit wood albedo: Λ (84,62,42) vs X (91,66,44), same hue ratios (r/g 1.36/1.38, g/b 1.45/1.49) — one wood. At the regime Λ reads L 73 r/g 1.74 against X's 47/1.63 because Λ is 1.4 tiles from the fire (reach 4.0) and X 6.3 — not the same fire. FIX: shift = cell − margin − PropBaseRun (one constant, shared with the occluder), so the base's far edge meets the foot and its near edge sits 11 px onto the floor; the cap-band re-lay removed. MEASURED AFTER (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/lambda/): flat-lit, the sprite's bottom wood row moved from 544 to 556 — 12 px, the 11.2-px run rounded to the pixel grid — so the base's far edge sits on the foot and its near edge 11 px onto the floor cell; the wall's foot line shows between the legs. No Tier1CapBand node exists (the counter is gone from the boundary line); the apex draws over the cap's near half and stops 12 px short of the cap's top. east_faces=5(ground-mask) unchanged. Albedo unchanged (no pixel of either sprite moved). JUDGE (Rafe, 2026-09-13): the fine fact — bottom row at foot + 12, zero cap pixels over the lower half — is the DERIVED ASSERTION this exit carries; the deck's grounding plant is the coarse failure (lambda-in-the-face).
item_exit.instrument: wood-pixel rows and flat-lit albedo (tools/cast_shadows/evidence/jamb/face_stats.py family), the [Tier1] boundary summary line; builder's measurements, none a gate

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
